text: Byrne's worked example comes from the qualitative phase of a mixed-methods study of Irish post-primary educators' attitudes toward promoting student social and emotional wellbeing. It used 11 semi-structured interviews lasting about 25–30 minutes, with core-curriculum teachers, wellbeing-curriculum teachers, pastoral-care members, and senior managers. These figures describe this one study, not a recommended sample size for reflexive thematic analysis. The author situated this example in interpretivism and constructivism and attended both to participants' accounts and to the researcher's interpretive role. The article says analysts should explain where they stand and why across four continua: essentialist–constructionist epistemology, experiential–critical orientation, inductive–deductive analysis, and semantic–latent coding, in relation to their research question. (Publisher PDF pp. 1394–1397.)
